title: Around the World
tagline: He bet his life — and lost it — on the shape of the Earth.

scenes.text: Seville, September 20, 1519. Five ships and 270 men set sail westward under a Portuguese captain sailing for Spain. Ferdinand Magellan's goal is the Spice Islands. His route: westward around South America, across an unknown ocean.

scenes.speaker: Magellan
scenes.text: They say the Pacific is weeks wide. I believe it may be months. I will not share that belief with the crew. Mutiny begins in the mind before it reaches the hands.

challenge.instruction: Before the five ships leave Seville, their holds must carry what the Spice Islands will take in trade for cloves. Stow the barter goods worth the most and leave the dead weight on the quay.
challenge.fact: Only 18 men completed the first circumnavigation, arriving back in Spain in September 1522 — three years after departing. Magellan himself was killed in the Philippines in April 1521, so he never finished the journey.

scenes.text: The Pacific crossing nearly destroyed them. 98 days without land. The crew ate leather from the rigging. Rats sold for half a gold ducat each. Twenty-nine men died of scurvy before they reached the Philippines.

scenes.speaker: Magellan
scenes.text: I did not come this far to turn back. Whatever lies ahead — it lies ahead. We sail.

challenge.instruction: Sort each port or landmark into the ocean Magellan's fleet crossed to reach it.
challenge.fact: Magellan named the Pacific Ocean 'Mar Pacífico' — the peaceful sea — after the violent storms of the strait that now bears his name. The irony was that the Pacific crossing nearly killed his crew from starvation.

scenes.text: On April 27, 1521, Magellan was killed in the Philippines — caught in a local dispute he chose to fight. He never finished his own circumnavigation. His one remaining ship did, arriving home with 18 survivors of the original 270.

challenge.instruction: Without their captain, the survivors reach Tidore and its cloves at last. Load the flagship's hold with the mix of spices that will pay for everything they have lost.
challenge.fact: At Tidore in November 1521 the two surviving ships, Trinidad and Victoria, took on cloves. The Trinidad sprang a leak and stayed behind for repairs; only the Victoria, under Juan Sebastián Elcano, sailed on west for Spain.

challenge.instruction: Elcano brings the Victoria home the long way, round Africa and clear of the Portuguese. Buy and sell at every landfall so the cargo is worth the lives it cost.
challenge.fact: The Victoria's cloves sold in Spain for more than the cost of the whole expedition. Charles V gave Elcano a coat of arms bearing a globe and the motto Primus circumdedisti me — 'You first went around me.'

scenes.speaker: Magellan
scenes.text: Lisbon is under Riot. At the end of every round, any side whose Strength totals under 5 is swept from the board. Francesco Borromini is already there and far too weak to last. Put me there and hold.

challenge.instruction: Fight lesson 4 · Survival. Deploy Magellan to Lisbon, keep at least 5 Strength there, and End Turn until two round endings have passed.
challenge.fact: A Local Survival event is a test, not a fight: at the end of each round every side at the location is checked, and a total under 5 loses every card there to the discard pile. Reinforce with followers, or retrieve a weak card before the round ends.
